scope: Independent read-only source review of the three concrete cancellation findings and directly affected regressions; separate from the management tests retained here.

findings.finding: Live operation identity initially lacked allocation handles, so a permissive prefix match could accept unpublished handles.
findings.resolution: Operation matching now requires the exact latest runtime identity. The live identity advances only after successful durable publication. The regression forges a previously empty AllocationID, and a separate case accepts the next legitimately published identity.

findings.finding: Current Deploy authority could change while the request waited for the product mutex, before gateway cancellation propagated to an isolated worker.
findings.resolution: The route rechecks request cancellation and current CaptureActor authority after the mutex wait. A separate live-context grant-change barrier covers this distinction; the backend owner preserved its original HTTP202 failure. Context cancellation alone is not claimed as sufficient authority proof.

findings.finding: Cancellation winning the final ready receipt could still return HTTP201 creation success.
findings.resolution: The final completion helper returns HTTP422 when the resulting receipt is not ready; the exact running identity, unknown outcome and Stop eligibility remain retained.

relatedReviewedCases: Cancellation route available while the exclusive source guard is held.
Cancelled and replaced source/allocation identities are refused without signalling or changing the receipt.
Closed publishers cannot rewrite retained uncertainty or reactivate on reopen.
One shutdown deadline bounds joining all active preview operations; cancellation does not itself release ledger capacity.
result: No outstanding source finding within this scope at the reviewed source hashes below. Backend race execution and integrated compilation belong to separate owner evidence; the management 11-outcome result does not establish them.
